updater._comment_endpoints: TODO (Phase 12, master prompt §62): this array is intentionally EMPTY — no real update-hosting endpoint exists yet, and this project deliberately does not fabricate a fake-but-plausible-looking one. Before this can ever check for a real update: host a `latest.json` manifest matching Tauri's updater manifest schema (https://v2.tauri.app/plugin/updater/#update-server-json-format) at a stable HTTPS URL, then put that real URL here as a single-element array, e.g. ["https://updates.yourdomain.example/ai-video-editor/{{target}}/{{arch}}/{{current_version}}"] — Tauri substitutes {{target}}/{{arch}}/{{current_version}} at check time. With this array empty, `commands::update::check_for_update` makes ZERO network requests (verified against tauri-plugin-updater 2.11.0's own source: an empty endpoints list skips its request loop and returns Err(ReleaseNotFound), surfaced honestly as UpdateCheckOutcome::CheckFailed) rather than silently succeeding or fabricating a result.
updater._comment_pubkey: TODO (Phase 12): placeholder — NOT a real key, cannot verify anything. A human must generate a real Ed25519 signing keypair once, on any machine that can run the Tauri CLI interactively (this WSL2 build container cannot do this non-interactively without inventing a fake key): run `pnpm dlx @tauri-apps/cli signer generate -w <path-to-save-private-key>` (e.g. `~/.tauri/ai-video-editor.key`), which prints the matching public key — paste that printed public key string in as the `pubkey` value below, and keep the generated private-key file secret (never commit it). Every release artifact referenced by the manifest above must then be signed with that same private key at release time via `pnpm dlx @tauri-apps/cli signer sign -k <private-key-path> <artifact-path>` (Tauri's bundler can also do this automatically during `tauri build` once `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`/`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` env vars are set to that key).
